title: Scientific verification: loss-curve shapes are diagnostic clues — analytic baselines, flat/explosion ambiguity, and documentation-verified clipping semantics

problem.description: EXP-000009 (latest version v3, content of the v2 technical revision) claims: (1) a loss-curve SHAPE is a clue that narrows to a candidate list, never a diagnosis by itself; (2) the loss VALUE relative to the analytic baseline disambiguates what the shape alone cannot — flat at ln(K) = not-learning, flat near zero = likely already fit, flat at the class-prior entropy = learned only the prior; (3) the quoted baseline numbers are exact (ln2=0.693147, ln10=2.302585, near-one-hot CE approaching 0); (4) for NaN/Inf-early curves the listed checks (input min/max scan, loss-formula audit, grad norms, LR probe) discriminate between a numeric loss fault and an LR fault; (5) framework clipping semantics are doc-verifiable. This run executes the record's own verification plan C1-C3 (C4 is practice-based and not mechanically testable, per the record itself), plus two cases verifying the rootCause's ambiguity claims (C5 flat-ambiguity, C6 explosion-ambiguity).
problem.symptoms: shotgun debugging during training misbehavior; acting on a loss-curve shape without a confirming check; misreading flat or exploding curves
problem.expectedBehavior: C1: -log(1/K) equals ln(K) exactly for K=2,10 and the CE of a constant p=1/K prediction equals ln(K). C2: the CE of a near-one-hot confident correct prediction approaches 0 (bounded by ~1-confidence). C5: three distinct causes (optimizer not stepping, broken graph, near-constant labels with uninformative inputs) all produce a FLAT curve; the first two sit at exactly ln(2)=0.693147 and are separated by the gradient/parameter-drift checks; the third converges to the class-prior entropy (~0.357), a different value — the VALUE splits the candidate space before any check runs. C6: a numeric loss fault (naive -log(p) underflow with clean inputs) and an LR fault (explosion at lr=1e4 with healthy step-0 loss) both produce NaN/Inf-early curves; the input scan, loss-formula audit and LR probe discriminate them. C3: the official PyTorch documentation states clip_grad_norm_ clips the gradient norm of an iterable of parameters, computes the norm as if concatenated into a single vector, and modifies gradients in place.
problem.actualBehavior: to be measured by real execution on the user's machine through the bridge
problem.facts: -log(1/K)=ln(K); the entropy of a 90/10 class prior is ~0.357 nats; naive -log(softmax) underflows to inf for logit gaps beyond ~745 while the log-sum-exp form stays finite; an LR of 1e4 amplifies a sane 0.122 gradient norm into a weight jump of ~1220 per step, driving the next step's loss to inf.
problem.assumptions: python3 3.14.4 on the user's machine; fixed seeds make every result deterministic; pure-python softmax regression substitutes framework training dynamics (torch absent on the workspace machine); outbound HTTPS available for the documentation check; pytorch.org may intermittently serve a bot-protection challenge on the stable path, so the doc case falls back to the versioned 2.15 URL resolved earlier the same day.
problem.environment: user's machine via the bridge extension: Linux, Python 3.14.4, torch absent; VM dry-runs on Python 3.12.16
problem.constraints: stdlib-only experiments; non-destructive (doc check writes only to mktemp); outputs below the 20KB truncation limit; the doc case fetches only official pytorch.org pages and is flagged requiresNetwork.

hypothesis.text: All five cases pass their declared criteria on real execution: the chance-floor baselines are exact; the confident-prediction CE approaches zero; the flat-curve ambiguity demonstration shows three causes with the value+checks separating them exactly as the record's triage method prescribes; the explosion ambiguity shows the loss-fault and LR-fault separated by the record's listed checks; and the live-fetched PyTorch documentation confirms the clipping semantics.
hypothesis.expectedObservation: markers: C1-CHANCE-FLOORS-VERIFIED, C2-CONFIDENT-CE-APPROACHES-ZERO, C5-VALUE-AND-CHECKS-DISAMBIGUATE, C6-CHECKS-DISAMBIGUATE, C3-DOC-VERIFIED
hypothesis.supportingEvidence: VM-local dry-runs (Python 3.12.16) reproduce every marker; design iterations (C2 threshold too strict at 1e-3; C6 initially crashed on math.log(0) and mislabeled sane norms as growing) were caught locally and corrected — the final C6 honestly reports sane norms and relies on elimination + the LR probe, exactly as the record's own check list prescribes.

strategy: Execute the record's plan C1/C2 (exact analytic baselines, deterministic), C5/C6 (ambiguity demonstrations implementing the record's triage method on pure-python training dynamics), C3 (live documentation inspection of clip_grad_norm_ semantics from the user's machine). C4 (shape->candidate mappings as practice-based priors) is deliberately NOT tested — the record itself classifies it as untested practice knowledge, and no source has been read to elevate it.
